product.subtitle: The Motion & Graphics Prompt Field Manual for Claude Code

mission.solves: You know what you want made. You do not know which prompt gets it made well. This manual routes any motion, graphic, video or ad job to a prompt with a known outcome, and tells you what to check before it goes out.
mission.who: Creators, marketers, teachers and small studios who direct the work and let Claude Code do the making. You need facts and taste. You do not need to code, animate or edit.
inside: 42 prompt cards across 8 kinds of work
4 levels, from one prompt to a full showcase pack
11 style lines, 20 add-on lines, 14 fix lines
3 checklists and a one-page cheat sheet
Real output pictured on 39 of the 42 cards

steps.title: Stage your files
steps.action: Make a project folder inside your workspace. Put every file the job needs in it: footage, logo, photos, notes. Copy the full path of the main file.
steps.why: The design apps cannot read outside the workspace, and Claude looks at every file before deciding anything. What a file shows outranks its name.
steps.tip: Use the original camera file. In one reference project the footage was a 464-pixel copy and stayed soft whatever was done to it.
steps.watch: Never hand over your only copy. Every prompt here says "never edit the original"; keep that line.

steps.title: Write the Six-Line Brief
steps.action: Fill in What, Who, Where, Must, Never and Ask me. Six lines. Paste them into the card's first prompt where its brackets ask for them.
steps.why: Every prompt that worked first time in the reference projects named the deliverable, the audience, the screen and the sound.
steps.tip: Type the Must facts exactly as they should read on screen. A date is printed as you typed it; a weekday is never worked out for you.
steps.watch: Whatever you leave out gets drafted for you: hooks, slogans, character names. Those drafts are yours to approve, not to assume.
steps.prompt: brief

steps.title: Set the dials
steps.action: Choose a level (Section 5), one style line and one delivery pack line. Add them to the prompt.
steps.why: The level decides how much you approve before the build. The pack line decides which files come back.
steps.tip: Default to L3 Storyboarded for anything a client or an algorithm will judge.
steps.watch: L4 Showcase multiplies the cost. Build one option, look at it, then ask for the rest.

steps.title: Diagnose first (existing work only)
steps.action: If you are improving something that already exists, ask what is holding it back before asking for anything new. Use card R1, step 0.
steps.why: The list of weaknesses becomes the brief for the storyboards.
steps.tip: Read the diagnosis and correct it. In the reference project one finding rested on a wrong assumption and was fixed in a sentence.
steps.watch: Skip this step for new work. It only adds time.

steps.title: Storyboard
steps.action: Run the card's storyboard prompt. A page opens with three options: frames, wording, timing, what each needs from you, and its risk.
steps.why: Three different films on paper cost a fraction of one built film.
steps.tip: Add: "Say honestly how each option copes with [MY WEAK POINT]." It surfaces the trade-off before you choose.
steps.watch: Three boards that differ only in colour are one idea. Send them back (Section 6 has the line).

steps.title: Choose or redirect
steps.action: Answer with a letter, a mix ("A's opening with C's ending"), a note on one frame, or a new direction for all three.
steps.why: In both real reference projects the direction changed here, in one sentence, before any build time was spent.
steps.tip: Read every on-screen line on the chosen board aloud. Change wording now.
steps.watch: Do not pick the prettiest frame. Pick the option a stranger would follow and remember.

steps.title: Build
steps.action: Run the card's build prompt with your delivery pack line. Ask for the report: the beats, the measured length and loudness, what could not be checked, the weakest part.
steps.why: The build follows the board you approved. The report tells you where to look first.
steps.tip: Need it silent in one place and loud in another? Add "Two versions: one silent, one with sound." now, not later.
steps.watch: Three options built at once hit a plan usage limit once in the reference projects. If a build stops, see Section 6.

steps.title: Watch and listen
steps.action: Play every file at full speed, with sound, on the kind of screen it is for.
steps.why: The build is checked by measurement: length, loudness, frames. Nobody has heard the mix or seen it move.
steps.tip: Check in this order: the first two seconds, every word on screen, the joins in any voice, the music, the last frame.
steps.watch: Read the credits file before commercial use. Music chosen from a catalogue may come with no licence text.

steps.title: Fix, re-version, file it
steps.action: Use a fix line for each problem. Then ask for the other sizes and versions. Then save the prompt that worked into your own notes.
steps.why: A new version never overwrites the old one, so every fix is safe. The prompt that worked is your next job's starting point.
steps.tip: One film that worked becomes a series with card R6.
steps.watch: One fix line, one problem. A list of ten changes gets nine of them.

cards.when: You filmed a product being used or explained (a book, a tool, a gadget) and want a TikTok that promotes by showing, not selling. Good for affiliate posts.

steps.label: Step 1 · Storyboards
steps.prompt:
/storyboard Three storyboards for a 15-second TikTok made from my raw video.

Source: [FULL PATH TO THE VIDEO]
It shows [WHAT IS ON SCREEN], with [WHOSE] voice explaining. The product is [EXACT PRODUCT NAME]. Work in that project folder and never edit the original.

Before proposing anything, analyse it properly:
- Go through the video frame by frame: what is on screen at each moment, and where the product itself appears.
- Transcribe the voice with word timings and match each sentence to what is on screen.
- Tell me which 15 seconds of material are strongest. Do not assume it is the first 15.

Every board must:
- open on the product itself, with hook words and an impactful effect in the first 2 seconds
- teach or show one real thing from the footage, clearly
- show why the product helps, using only what is visible in the footage
- end on the product with a closing line
- say NOTHING about price, buying, discounts or links
- use [LANGUAGE] on-screen text, vertical 1080x1920, exactly 15.0 seconds with all of it used, text clear of TikTok's buttons and caption area
- use the voice as the main sound

Make the three boards a real choice: three different hooks and three different ways of showing it. Say honestly how each copes with the quality of my footage.

Present the three, recommend one, and stop for my choice.

steps.label: Step 2 · Build the one you chose
steps.prompt:
/studio start the [PROJECT NAME] project from its chosen storyboard.

Motion: lively and interesting to watch. Something moves at all times, text lands on the spoken word, and the finish on the product is satisfying.

Voice: it sounds slow and is quiet. Improve it in this order and stop as soon as it sounds natural: cut the pauses between phrases (never mid-word); speed it up a little without changing pitch (no more than about 1.15x, and tell me the exact figure); bring it up to normal TikTok loudness. No AI voice, noise removal or voice separation. Keep a copy of the untouched voice so I can compare.

Add soft sound effects on visible actions and light music under the voice, free to use and credited.

Deliver the MP4, a cover image and a small copy for messaging apps. Report the beats, exactly what you did to the voice, the measured length and loudness, and anything you could not check.

Listen before posting. The joins in the voice are placed by measurement; nobody has heard them.

cards.title: Routine film for children, with on-screen dialogue
cards.when: A calm film that shows children doing a routine (tidying, bedtime, getting ready for school), played on a TV, often with no sound.
cards.get: Three storyboards with every line of dialogue and its on-screen time, then one continuous film that loops.

steps.label: Step 1 · Storyboards
steps.prompt:
/storyboard Storyboards for a calming cartoon for young children: [WHO, e.g. three siblings] [DO WHAT ROUTINE] before [WHAT]. A child watching should want to do the same.

Where it plays: [LIVING-ROOM TV / TABLET], with [NO sound / sound]. Everything must make sense without sound and to a child who cannot read yet.

Characters: [NAMES, WHO IS ELDEST, ANYTHING ABOUT HOW THEY LOOK].
Dialogue: short, warm lines in [LANGUAGE], shown on screen, large enough to read from the sofa. [WHERE THERE MUST BE NO DIALOGUE].
Fixed: 16:9 using the whole frame, a seamless loop of about [120] seconds, a playful opening that settles into a calm pace.

ASK ME before you draw [THE PART ONLY I CAN DECIDE].

Make the three boards a real choice: who leads the story, how many words, how the camera moves. Write every line on the frame where it appears, with how long it stays up. Present the three, recommend one, and stop for my choice.

steps.label: Step 2 · Build with a full pack
steps.prompt: /studio start the [PROJECT NAME] project from its chosen storyboard. Two versions: one silent, one with sound. Deliver each at 3840x2160 and 1920x1080, each exactly one loop.

tips: Anything cultural or religious that must be right: put it under ASK ME and check the frames yourself.
A long film with dialogue runs longer than you expect: every line needs reading time. In the reference project a 120-second plan became 150.

steps.label: Step 0 · Ask for a diagnosis
steps.prompt: I want to improve an existing video to the best quality. It is at [FULL PATH]. The goal is [WHAT IT SHOWS AND WHO IT IS FOR]. It will be played [WHERE], [WITH / WITHOUT] sound. Look at it first, tell me what is holding it back, then give me a prompt.

steps.label: Step 1 · Storyboards
steps.prompt:
/storyboard Storyboards for a better version of an existing film. Do not edit or overwrite the original.

Source: [FULL PATH]
Look at the whole film first (a frame every 2 seconds) and use its [SETTING, CHARACTERS AND STORY] as the starting point. Work in that same project folder.

What it is for: [PURPOSE, AUDIENCE, WHERE IT PLAYS, SOUND OR NO SOUND].
New in this version: [WHAT TO ADD, e.g. dialogue in English shown on screen].
Fixed in all three boards: [WHAT MUST STAY THE SAME].

Every board must also fix what is weak in the current film:
- [PASTE THE LIST FROM STEP 0]

ASK ME before you draw [THE PART ONLY I CAN DECIDE].

Make the three boards a real choice, not only a change of colour. Present the three, recommend one, and stop for my choice. Do not build the film.

steps.label: Step 2 · Build with a full pack
steps.prompt: /studio start the [PROJECT NAME] project from its chosen storyboard. Two versions: one silent, one with sound. Deliver the silent MP4 at 3840x2160 and 1920x1080, the sound version at the same sizes, each exactly one loop, and a before/after sheet against the original film.

tips: Step 0 matters: the list of weaknesses it produces becomes the brief for the boards. Correct anything in it that is wrong before you paste it on.
Drop the 4K size if your player stutters, and "each exactly one loop" if the film does not loop.
